key_insight: Boosting noisy quantum classifiers can achieve a shared classification target with fewer circuit executions than probabilistic error cancellation, avoiding full reconstruction of ideal outputs.
engineering_relevance: For supervised quantum classification, task-aware ensembles may reduce sampling costs by exploiting predictive information that survives hardware noise.
method: Compare boosting and probabilistic error cancellation against the same learning target.
Bound hypothesis-class complexity for specified circuit architectures under Pauli noise, linking matched empirical margin loss to a shared risk upper bound.
Evaluate AdaBoostR and Real AdaBoost in finite-shot teacher–student simulations.
evidence_signal: Across simulated circuit depths and physical noise strengths, boosting required fewer executions at the same accuracy target as depth and noise increased, and achieved higher test accuracy than the corresponding reference.
watch_item: The reported advantage is task-dependent and demonstrated in specified simulated settings; broader applicability and hardware performance remain unestablished.
paper_title: Beyond Error Mitigation: Using Boosting for Noisy Quantum Machine Learning
